title: Alivus Life Sciences Ltd - 543322 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Alivus FY26 revenue rose 6.9% to INR2,552 crore, with EBITDA up 19.6% to INR858 crore and a record 33.6% margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR689 crore (+6.1% YoY) with EBITDA of INR237 crore (+13.8%, 34.4% margin) and PAT of INR163 crore. FY26 PAT was INR565 crore (22.1% margin), and non-GPL revenue, now 71% of the total, grew 13%. Management flagged a Dahej fire (INR20 crore loss booked in other expenses), freight and solvent cost pass-through, and Solapur Phase 1 commissioning in Q2 FY27 as the main near-term items. FY27 capex is planned at about INR540 crore, funded entirely from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 gross profit / gross margin

financial_highlights.change: +19.6% YoY; margin +360 bps, highest in company history

financial_highlights.value: INR91 crore (3.6% of sales); Q4 INR25 crore (3.6%)

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 capex / cash and equivalents at 31 Mar 2026
financial_highlights.value: INR306 crore capex / INR782 crore cash
INR31 crore for FY26 (INR20 crore in FY26 per split, INR11 crore in Q4)

segments.name: Non-GPL business
segments.commentary: Contributed 71% of FY26 revenue, up from 59% in FY22; non-GPL revenue grew 13% in FY26 and at a 7.5% CAGR over FY24–FY26. Management expects its share to keep rising.

segments.name: GPL business
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable over the past two years; management described it as wavy and does not expect it to track non-GPL growth.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Recovered from Q3 FY26; share of revenue rose from 6% in FY25 to 7% in FY26, and management said CDMO has better margins. Projects four and five have ramped up; two new deals are expected in early H2 FY27.

segments.name: Therapy mix
segments.commentary: CVS and CNS each contributed 50% of the top line; respiratory and anti-allergy together exceed 10% of revenue. Chronic therapies were 67% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: High-potency API
segments.commentary: 28 products in pipeline: 12 validated, 7 advanced, 9 in land development. Revenue so far is only exhibit-batch sales; meaningful contribution is expected from FY28 as patents expire in early 2028.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to be sustained in the 30%–32% range; management said it is too early to give full-year margin guidance given the war-related supply constraints.
Solapur Phase 1 (370 KL BI block and 120 KL API block) to be operational in Q2 FY27; initial utilisation of 40%–50%, rising to 60%–70% the following year.
Brownfield capacity expected to reach 80%–90% utilisation within 2–3 quarters of start-up.
FY27 capex of about INR540 crore, including FY26 carryover, fully funded from internal accruals.
Capacity to rise from 1,198 KL in FY24 to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28.
R&D intensity expected to reach about 4% of sales in the next year or two and not cross 4%.
Asset turnover expected to fall temporarily below 2x as Solapur and brownfield capacity come online.
Price erosion of about 4.5% overall and 5.5% in non-GPL, non-CDMO; price increases being passed on to customers for freight and solvent costs.
capex_capacity: Solapur Phase 1 is on track for Q2 FY27 operations; backward integration projects are expected to follow once Solapur is online, with some benefit in H2.
Solapur sits on 40 acres and could add another 700–800 KL of API capacity; Solapur is currently at 120 KL for API.
Ankleshwar contributes about 65%–70% of revenue and has room to expand, but management will go slowly there; Dahej is full.
New R&D centre at Taloja, Navi Mumbai is under construction.
Dahej fire affected only the intermediate section; API and finished-goods areas were intact, with limited spillover expected into Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth is described as strong across all segments; pricing is reasonably stable because the portfolio is newer and less commoditised.
Solvents (about 12%–13% of cost) rose sharply from 28 February 2026 with freight; customers are largely accepting pass-through of material and freight costs.
Operations cost is stable after moving from gas to briquette boilers, insulating costs from gas shortages.
Customers have accepted reasonable price increases; contracts are mostly short (1–2 years) for generic API, while CDMO contracts are longer-term.
Generic API launches in several markets supported margins; management said new launches are not a significant contributor to top-line growth yet.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Dahej fire on production, sales and P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the intermediate area was hit; limited spillover into Q1. INR20 crore fire loss booked in other expenses. Employee cost rise reflects accrued performance bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Forex gains and gross margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Net forex gain of INR31 crore in P&L for FY26, of which INR11 crore in Q4 and about INR20 crore cited for the full year in the answer. Company is a net exporter, so rupee depreciation helps.

qa_highlights.question: Price erosion in the base business excluding GPL and CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5.5% for non-GPL, non-CDMO; about 4.5% across the overall bucket. Management expects base business growth of the same kind to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for capacity utilisation of new facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Brownfield to 80%–90% in 2–3 quarters; Solapur to start at 40%–50%, then 60%–70% the following year. Solapur's 370 KL BI block is for backward integration and should not be modelled as front-end sales.

qa_highlights.question: R&D trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D spend is rising, focused on flow chemistry, high-potency APIs, pellets and granules (API plus), and CDMO; management does not expect R&D to exceed 4% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the two CDMO contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may come in the first half, a little later than before, but is guiding to the early part of H2 FY27 to be safe.

risks_watch: Geopolitical conflict and freight/raw material cost inflation; management expects pass-through but acknowledges some raw materials may rise further.
Solapur commissioning in Q2 FY27 and regulatory inspection, which is needed before Solapur can supply regulated markets and the planned expansion can proceed.
High-potency API revenue is negligible until patent expiries in early 2028, so the margin benefit is deferred.
Two CDMO deal closings slipped from the earlier June–July timeframe to early H2 FY27.
Asset turnover is set to fall below 2x temporarily; ramp-up pace of new capacity determines returns.
Price erosion of about 4.5%–5.5% in parts of the portfolio; GPL remains volatile.
Management did not quantify new-launch contribution to FY26 revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and cash, but cautious on the near-term outlook. Management was guarded on the war's impact on supply chains and margins, declined to give full-year margin guidance, and moderated the CDMO timing. It was evasive on the new-launch revenue split.
key_quotes: The partnership with Nirma brought enhanced financial strength, long-term stability and greater flexibility to invest in future growth opportunities.
And growth will come. I'm not saying that growth will not come, but growth will not be pursued at the cost of margins because it creates a lot of other challenges then.
Solapur is on 40 acres, and we would comfortably be able to add another 700 to 800 kiloliters of capacity of API capacity in Solapur.

growth.why: Management guided EBITDA margin to 30-32% and FY27 capex of about INR540 crore funded internally, with Solapur Phase 1 (370 KL BI, 120 KL API) operational in Q2 FY27 at 40-50% initial utilisation; revenue growth is not explicitly guided and the 6.1% Q4 growth and 6.9% FY26 growth are the only hard numbers, with volume growth described as strong but no order book quantified.
